data.narrative:
ISEE, a Series B drone and autonomous systems company founded by Yibiao Zhao, has raised $70M to date. The broader sector comprises eight private peers, including Elroy Air, Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, and Joby Aviation, with no public comparables available. Public markets offer limited direct benchmarking in this nascent category.

Valuation analysis relied on the Stage-Progression method, the sole applicable triangulation approach. This method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $70M total capital raised as a proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $133M. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while seven same-sector peers exist, none met the filtering criteria for meaningful comparison (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), resulting in an insufficient narrow peer set of fewer than three datapoints. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity within Drones & Autonomous.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $113M (low) to $153M (high), with a midpoint of $133M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty. The range reflects ±15% variance around the median to capture execution risk and market volatility. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of historical stage-step multipliers for this sector, the absence of recent comparable transactions at ISEE's stage, and rapid technology-driven valuation variance in autonomous systems. Additional market data or transaction comps would materially improve confidence in this assessment.
